target_customer: Limited partners and investors who would allocate capital to an AI run hedge fund
problem: Hedge funds rely on human generated trading hypotheses, and Pit.AI wanted machine learning to find and judge strategies automatically.
business_model: Hedge fund managing outside capital, planned carry based fees

founders.name: Yves-Laurent Kom Samo
prior_employers: Google (described as a Google Fellow by TechCrunch)
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch 2017 gives the Oxford PhD and Google. A secondary dead startups site adds Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan roles, not confirmed on a primary source. He later founded KXY Technologies per that site.

exit.reason: No public statement; a secondary site says it closed quietly in early 2021

competitors.name: Quantopian
competitors.what: Crowdsourced quant algorithm platform and fund

technical_complexity.rationale: Applying reinforcement learning to evaluate strategies on noisy financial data is research grade, and TechCrunch notes the fund had not yet raised LP capital.

defensibility.rationale: Research know how could lead to proprietary strategies, but a track record was missing and rivals had crowds and more resources.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source says rivals bought or copied Pit.AI. Pit.AI did not reach a public track record.

market_need_then: TechCrunch 2017 notes interest in machine learning hedge funds and a crowd of competing quant efforts, but no LP demand data. Pit.AI had not raised from LPs by March 2017.

branding.domain_note: Held pit.ai; the domain now redirects to a GoDaddy for sale page, per the fetch.
branding.community_and_virality: A research paper series was launched in 2018 per a secondary site.

brand_strength.rationale: Coverage was limited to TechCrunch at Demo Day. The name later collided with an unrelated 2026 company called Pit.

outcome_analysis: Pit.AI joined YC in Winter 2017 as a hedge fund using reinforcement learning, with a PhD founder and about 120000 of seed money, and had not raised LP capital at Demo Day. A secondary site says it closed quietly in early 2021 after struggling to raise LP money without a live track record and finding financial signal harder to extract than expected. No primary shutdown statement exists, so these factors are a best reading from one secondary source.
notes: pit.ai redirects to a domain for sale page, so the site is dead. The 120000 seed rests on CB Insights (investors Y Combinator and Entrepreneurs First) and a secondary site that names Zillionize instead of Entrepreneurs First; conflict unresolved. Shutdown timing and causes rest on one secondary site. Results about a Stockholm company called Pit that raised 16M in 2026 are unrelated.
